#### Pacific Highlands Ranch

6 communities · 256 homes

The newest part of Carmel Valley, built out from the 2000s onward, and home to Canyon Crest Academy. Its condos and townhomes are newer construction; check each community's Mello-Roos tax along with the HOA fee.

#### Torrey Hills

2 communities · 225 homes

South of SR-56, Torrey Hills is close to Sorrento Valley and the I-5/I-805 merge. It has two condo and townhome communities among its single-family neighborhoods.

- **San Raphael** — 125 homes · Detached condos
- **Sausalito** — 100 homes · Detached condos

### How to Choose a Carmel Valley Condo Community

Start with location, then compare what you pay each month and what you get for it. Two homes at the same price can cost very different amounts to own once monthly dues and Mello-Roos are added, and a community’s age, size and layout shape day-to-day life more than its name does.

#### Area and commute

Communities south of Del Mar Heights Road are closest to the shops, offices and I-5/SR-56. Pacific Highlands Ranch is newer and further east; Torrey Hills sits near Sorrento Valley.

#### Condo or townhome

Condos are often single-level with shared walls above or below. Townhomes usually have two or more levels, an attached garage and no one overhead.

#### Full monthly cost

Add the monthly dues, any Mello-Roos tax and property tax to the mortgage. Newer communities often carry Mello-Roos; older ones may have lower dues but older systems.

#### Schools

Most of Carmel Valley is in the Del Mar Union and San Dieguito Union districts, but school assignment depends on the address. Each community guide lists its schools.

#### Size and turnover

Larger communities have more sales each year, so prices are easier to compare and there is more to choose from. Smaller ones come up less often.

#### Rules and amenities

Pools, gyms, pet rules and rental limits differ by community. Ask for the HOA documents before you commit, and check the reserves.

### Carmel Valley Communities: Common Questions

#### How many condo and townhome communities are in Carmel Valley?

This map shows 41 condo and townhome communities in Carmel Valley (San Diego, 92130), with more than 5,700 homes between them. They are spread across 5 areas, and 23 of them are south of Del Mar Heights Road.

#### Which part of Carmel Valley has the most condos?

South of Del Mar Heights Road. It has 23 of the 41 condo and townhome communities on this map, so it usually has the most listings and the widest range of sizes and prices.

#### What are the largest condo communities in Carmel Valley?

By number of homes, the largest are Pell Place (317 homes), Camino Villas (316 homes), East Bluff (306 homes). Bigger communities tend to have more sales each year, which makes prices easier to compare.

#### Are there newer condos and townhomes in Carmel Valley?

Yes. Pacific Highlands Ranch, in the east of Carmel Valley, was built out from the 2000s onward, so its attached homes are newer. Many communities there carry a Mello-Roos tax on top of the HOA fee, so compare the full monthly cost.

#### Is there a list of every condo community in Carmel Valley?

Yes. The list beside the map on this page has all 41 condo and townhome communities in Carmel Valley, grouped by area, with their type and number of homes. Open an area, then tap a community to see it on the map.

#### How do I find out what is for sale in a specific community?

Tap the community on the map, then See homes. Where we have a community guide, it shows live listings, recent sales, monthly dues and schools. For any other community, call or email Sez Sezer for current listings and recent sales.

*Good to Know*

### Carmel Valley Condo FAQs

#### What is the price range for condos in Carmel Valley?

Pricing varies by community, size, and age. Entry-level condos typically start in the mid-to-high range for the 92130 zip, while larger and newer luxury residences near One Paseo command a premium. Reach out for a current, community-specific price breakdown.

#### What do HOA fees typically cover?

Most Carmel Valley condo HOAs cover exterior maintenance, common-area landscaping, insurance for shared structures, and amenities such as pools or fitness centers. Fees and inclusions differ by community — I can provide the specifics for any community you're considering.

#### Are Carmel Valley condos a good investment?

Carmel Valley's top-rated schools, coastal access, and steady demand have historically supported strong long-term value. Condos appeal to both lifestyle buyers and investors seeking lower-maintenance ownership in a premium San Diego submarket.

#### How competitive is the Carmel Valley condo market?

Well-priced condos in desirable communities often move quickly. Working with a local specialist who sees new inventory early — and understands each HOA — gives you a meaningful edge.

*Good to Know*

### Carmel Valley Townhome FAQs

#### What is the price range for townhomes in Carmel Valley?

Pricing varies by community, size, and age. Entry-level townhomes typically start in the mid-to-high range for the 92130 zip, while larger and newer residences in gated communities near One Paseo command a premium. Reach out for a current, community-specific price breakdown.

#### What's the difference between a condo and a townhome here?

In Carmel Valley the distinction is often about ownership structure rather than appearance. Townhomes frequently include the land beneath the unit, while condos typically involve ownership of the interior unit with shared common areas. MLS listings sometimes use the terms interchangeably, so it's worth confirming the specifics of any property.

#### What do HOA fees typically cover?

Most Carmel Valley townhome HOAs cover exterior maintenance, common-area landscaping, insurance for shared structures, and amenities such as pools or fitness centers. Fees and inclusions differ by community — I can provide the specifics for any community you're considering.

#### How competitive is the Carmel Valley townhome market?

Well-priced townhomes in desirable communities often move quickly, especially larger floor plans near top-rated schools. Working with a local specialist who sees new inventory early — and understands each HOA — gives you a meaningful edge.

### What a 1-Bed vs. a 2-Bed Actually Costs

Arborlake has only 1- and 2-bedroom floor plans. Here's what each has sold for recently: the last 12 months, or a longer window where fewer than three sold.

#### 1 Bedroom

last 3 sales · since May 2023

- **Size:** 742–896 sq ft
- **Median sale price:** $640,000
- **Price range:** $600K–$685K

#### 2 Bedroom

5 sales · 24 mo

- **Size:** 964–1,071 sq ft
- **Median sale price:** $820,000
- **Price range:** $756K–$900K

Over the last 5 years, two-bedrooms have sold nearly three times as often as one-bedrooms — a narrower buyer pool for the smaller units usually means more negotiating room if a 1-bed is what you're after. See the [full breakdown](https://www.carmelvalleycondos.com/arborlake-carmel-valley/#analysis).

Closed MLS sales, last 5 years.

### Life at Arborlake

A 190-unit condo community in southwest Carmel Valley, built by Baldwin Homes in 1986–1989 around a central lake, fountains, waterfalls and greenbelt walking paths. Most patios and balconies face the water and landscaping, not the parking. See the full [Arborlake community profile](https://www.carmelvalley.com/condos-for-sale/arborlake/).

#### Why buyers choose Arborlake

- **The lake & water features.** A central lake with fountains and waterfalls that no newer 92130 community has room for.
- **Resort-style amenities.** Two lighted tennis courts, a heated pool, two spas, a sauna and a fitness center, all HOA-maintained.
- **Mature, walkable grounds.** Nearly 40 years of tree canopy, greenbelts and paved walking paths.

*HOA*

### Arborlake Monthly Dues & Amenities

One monthly fee covers the lake, the amenities and the outside of every building.

$450–$460/month

**HOA fee** 2025–2026 MLS listings show $450–$460 for 1- and 2-bedrooms alike. Much of it maintains the lake, fountains and waterfalls.

#### Amenities included

- Lake, fountains & waterfalls
- Heated pool & two spas
- Sauna & fitness center
- Two lighted tennis courts
- Greenbelts & walking paths
- Covered carports & storage

**Also covered:** exterior building maintenance and all greenbelt landscaping.

#### How the Monthly Dues Compare

- **The Lakes:** $560–$599/mo
- **Martinique:** $428–$500/mo
- **Arborlake:** $450–$460/mo
- **Camino Villas:** $375–$450/mo
- **Carmel Pointe:** $340–$433/mo
- **Del Mar Villas:** $330–$370/mo

Ranges are from 2025–2026 MLS listings. Arborlake sits in the middle: below The Lakes, above Carmel Pointe and Del Mar Villas.

#### Del Mar Villas

#### Five Years of Arborlake Sales: What the Data Shows

Written November 2026 from 22 closed sales (late 2021–2026). The other tabs update automatically.

- **Price per square foot is rising.** It climbed two years running, to about $815/sq ft in 2025 and $833/sq ft in 2026, a steadier signal than the median price.
- **2-bedrooms are the main market.** 16 of the 22 sales were 2-bedrooms. 1-bedrooms sell less often, which usually means more room to negotiate.
- **Well-priced units sell fast again.** 2025 sales averaged 6 days on market, down from 62 days in 2024.

#### The Big Picture: 22 Sales in Five Years

Between late 2021 and today, 22 Arborlake condos have closed escrow. That's not a large sample — some years saw as few as one or two sales, so 2021 and 2024 in particular are single data points, not statistically reliable averages — so the year-by-year numbers in the Overview tab are best read as a trend, not a guarantee. Still, the trend is legible: after a dip through 2022–2023, median prices have climbed in each of the last two full years.

#### Price Per Square Foot Is the Steadier Signal

Median price swings around in a market this small — a single larger or smaller unit selling in a given year can shift the headline number by tens of thousands of dollars. Price per square foot is a cleaner read, because it adjusts for exactly that. And on that measure, Arborlake's story is less bumpy than the median-price table suggests: a climb from $663/sq ft in 2021 to the $770s through 2022–2023, a dip in 2024, and then a clear move upward to $815/sq ft in 2025 and $833/sq ft so far in 2026.

Two consecutive years of rising price per square foot, even while the raw median bounced around, is the more trustworthy signal that Arborlake values are genuinely appreciating — not just that bigger units happened to sell.

#### A Tale of Two Unit Types

Arborlake's 1-bedroom and 2-bedroom units have moved differently enough over the last five years that lumping them into one number hides more than it reveals.

- **2-bed median · 16 sales · $675K–$900K range:** $800,000
- **1-bed median · 6 sales · $578K–$815K range:** $631,750

Two-bedroom units have been the steadier performer: 16 closings, a tight-ish range, and a trend line that points up across the five-year window. One-bedrooms are a different story — only six sales, a wider spread relative to their price point, and a flatter-to-slightly-declining trend. Some of that gap is a sample-size artifact (six sales is not much to draw a line through), but some of it likely reflects genuine demand: two-bedroom units suit a broader range of buyers — downsizers who still want a guest room, small families, investors targeting a wider renter pool — while one-bedrooms draw a narrower, more price-sensitive buyer. The one outlier worth noting: a 1-bedroom sold for $815,000 in the dataset, well above the 1-bed median, almost certainly reflecting an upgraded or larger-than-typical unit rather than a shift in the baseline 1-bed market.

#### Days on Market Tell Their Own Story

If price is what a home sold for, days on market is how hard the seller had to work for it. Arborlake's pattern here is noisy — again, small numbers — but the direction lines up with the price data: 2025's four sales averaged just 6 days on market, among the fastest of the five-year window, while 2024's two sales (one of which sat 79 days) averaged 62. That's consistent with a market that cooled into 2023–2024 and has since tightened back up, rewarding well-priced, well-presented units with quick sales again.

#### How the HOA Fits Into the Value Picture

None of this happens in a vacuum. Arborlake's HOA is $450–$460/month in 2025–2026 MLS listings — above Carmel Pointe and Del Mar Villas, below The Lakes — and that fee buys something those comparables don't have: a maintained central lake with fountains and waterfalls, two tennis courts, a heated pool, two spas, a sauna, and a fitness center. The price and $/sq ft trends in the other tabs suggest the market has been willing to pay for that, not penalize it — appreciation has continued with the HOA where it is.

#### What This Means If You're Buying or Selling

**If you're buying:** don't anchor too hard to any single closed sale — with this few transactions a year, one unusually large or small unit can swing the "median" meaningfully. Price per square foot and the direction of days-on-market are more reliable signals than any one closing. And know that 2-bedroom units have a longer, steadier sales history to lean on than 1-bedrooms do.

**If you're selling:** the data says pricing discipline matters more now than it did in the slower 2023–2024 stretch. The fastest, highest sales in this dataset — several under 10 days on market in 2025 — went to units priced right and presented well from day one, not to units that started high and chased the market down.

### Is Arborlake the Right Community for You?

Who it suits best, and the honest tradeoffs to weigh before you buy.

#### A great fit for

- **Setting-Driven Buyers** — Lake views and mature landscaping no comparable 92130 condo offers at this price.
- **Downsizers** — Pool, spa and sauna a short walk away, and no yard to maintain.
- **Investors** — No Mello-Roos keeps carrying costs predictable for long-term holds.

#### Tradeoffs to weigh

- **Carport parking, not a garage** — Covered carport with storage, but no enclosed garage.
- **Floor plans vary by building** — Some units have stairs. Confirm the floor level and elevator access.
- **HOA covers the exterior, not the interior** — Kitchens, baths and flooring are the owner's job. Ask about a unit's updates.
- **No private yard** — Outdoor space is a patio or balcony. Lake-facing units are the most sought after.

*Good to Know*

### Arborlake Carmel Valley FAQs

#### What is the price range for Arborlake condos?

Recent sales at Arborlake ranged from about $600,000 to $900,000. By size: 1-bedrooms $600K–$685K (median $640K; the last 3 sales, since May 2023) and 2-bedrooms $756K–$900K (median $820K; 5 sales in the last 24 months). Condition, floor level and location in the community explain most of the gap. Ask for a current comparison before you make an offer.

#### What do the monthly dues at Arborlake cover?

Arborlake's HOA is $450–$460 per month in 2025–2026 MLS listings and covers the community's central lake and fountain system, two lighted tennis courts, a heated pool, two spas, a dry sauna, a fitness center, all greenbelt landscaping, exterior building maintenance, and covered carport parking with storage.

#### Does Arborlake have Mello-Roos?

No — Arborlake carries no Mello-Roos assessment, with a property tax rate of approximately 1.07% of assessed value.

#### How big are the units at Arborlake?

Arborlake units range from 742-square-foot one-bedrooms to 1,145-square-foot two-bedroom layouts.

#### How does Arborlake compare to other Carmel Valley condo communities?

Arborlake's HOA ($450–$460/mo) sits between The Lakes ($560–$599/mo) and Carmel Pointe ($340–$433/mo) or Del Mar Villas ($330–$370/mo). Much of it funds the central lake, fountains and waterfalls that most nearby communities don't have.

#### How quickly do Arborlake condos sell?

Well-priced, updated listings typically go under contract within 2–3 weeks, reflecting a buyer pool that often targets this specific community rather than comparison-shopping broadly.

#### What should I check when I tour an Arborlake condo?

1. **Which way it faces:** patio or balcony toward the lake and landscaping, or toward parking. It's the biggest value driver.
2. **Floor level and stairs:** ground-floor walk-up or upstairs, and elevator access for that building.
3. **Amenity noise:** units near the tennis courts or pool hear weekend activity.
4. **Age of systems:** water heater, HVAC and plumbing updates. The buildings date to 1986–1989.
5. **Carport and storage:** which space and storage unit convey, and how far they are from the door.

### Life at Carmel Pointe

A 200-unit condo community built by Western Pacific Housing in 2001–2002, set in a quiet pocket that's still a short walk from Del Mar Highlands Town Center and One Paseo. High ceilings, private patios or decks, and underground and garage parking set it apart from older Carmel Valley condos.

#### Why buyers choose Carmel Pointe

- **Walk to shopping and dining.** Del Mar Highlands Town Center is about a 5-minute walk, with One Paseo just beyond.
- **Garage parking, not carports.** Underground and garage parking come with the home, which is rare among Carmel Valley condos of this age.
- **Resort-style amenities.** An oversized pool, hydrotherapy spa, fitness center, clubhouse and BBQ area, all HOA-maintained.

*HOA*

### Carmel Pointe Monthly Dues & Amenities

One monthly fee covers the amenities, the grounds, and utilities most HOAs bill separately.

$340–$433/month

**HOA fee** Depends on size: about $340–$355 for 1-bedrooms and $387–$433 for 2-bedrooms in 2025–2026 MLS listings. Lower than Arborlake and The Lakes, and it includes water, sewer, trash and hot water.

#### Amenities included

- Oversized pool & spa
- Fitness center
- Clubhouse & rec room
- BBQ & outdoor area
- Underground & garage parking
- Walking & biking trail access

**Also covered:** water, sewer, trash and hot water, plus landscaping and common-area upkeep.

#### How the Monthly Dues Compare

- **The Lakes:** $560–$599/mo
- **Martinique:** $428–$500/mo
- **Arborlake:** $450–$460/mo
- **Camino Villas:** $375–$450/mo
- **Carmel Pointe:** $340–$433/mo
- **Del Mar Villas:** $330–$370/mo

Ranges are from 2025–2026 MLS listings. Counting the utilities it covers, Carmel Pointe's real monthly cost is lower than the fee alone suggests.

### Is Carmel Pointe the Right Community for You?

Who it suits best, and the honest tradeoffs to weigh before you buy.

#### A great fit for

- **Relocating Professionals** — Garage parking, a full gym and walkable shopping, with SR-56 and I-5 close by.
- **First-Time Buyers** — A 92130 address and top-rated schools, with water, sewer and trash already in the HOA.
- **Investors** — Steady rental demand near Del Mar Highlands, and a utility-inclusive HOA keeps costs predictable.

#### Tradeoffs to weigh

- **Shared garage, not a private one** — Parking is underground or in shared garage structures, not an attached private garage.
- **Compact floor plans** — Most homes are 1- and 2-bedrooms under 1,200 sq ft. 3-bedrooms are rare.
- **Few sales to compare** — Only about 5 homes a year sell here, so good units go fast and recent comps are thin.
- **Interiors vary** — Some units still have their original 2002 finishes. Ask what's been updated.

*Good to Know*

### Carmel Pointe Carmel Valley FAQs

#### What is the price range for Carmel Pointe condos?

Recent sales at Carmel Pointe ranged from about $540,000 to $995,000. By size: 1-bedrooms $540K–$575K (median $575K; 3 sales in the last 12 months), 2-bedrooms $725K–$863K (median $835K; 4 sales in the last 24 months) and 3-bedrooms $970K–$995K (median $970K; the last 3 sales, since Nov 2023). Condition, floor level and location in the community explain most of the gap. Ask for a current comparison before you make an offer.

#### What do the monthly dues at Carmel Pointe cover?

The HOA is $340–$433 per month in 2025–2026 MLS listings: about $340–$355 for 1-bedrooms and $387–$433 for 2-bedrooms. It covers the pool, spa, fitness center, clubhouse, landscaping and common areas, plus water, sewer, trash and hot water.

#### Does Carmel Pointe have Mello-Roos?

Yes. In 2025–2026 MLS listings, most Carmel Pointe units show a Mello-Roos (CFD) assessment of about $366–$564 per year, a median of about $457 (roughly $38 a month). The base property tax rate is about 1.1% of assessed value. Check the exact amount for a specific unit on its tax bill.

#### How big are the units at Carmel Pointe?

From about 704 sq ft (1-bedroom) to 1,387 sq ft (3-bedroom). Most sales were 2-bedrooms between about 960 and 1,190 sq ft.

#### What is parking like at Carmel Pointe?

Parking is underground and in garages rather than surface carports. Ask which space conveys with a specific unit.

#### How quickly do Carmel Pointe condos sell?

About 5 homes sell here a year. Over the last 5 years the median time on market was about 5 weeks; well-priced, updated units often go faster.

#### How does Carmel Pointe compare to other Carmel Valley condo communities?

Carmel Pointe (2001–2002) is newer than neighboring Arborlake (1986–1989) and The Lakes, has garage parking instead of carports, and its HOA ($340–$433/mo) is lower while also covering utilities.

### Thinking About Carmel Pointe?

Closed MLS sales, last 5 years.

### Life at The Lakes

Built by Baldwin Homes in 1984–1985, The Lakes is set around five small lakes connected by streams, with koi and lily ponds, grassy walkways and four decades of mature trees. It's one of the most affordable ways into a 92130 address, with no Mello-Roos. See the full [The Lakes community profile](https://www.carmelvalley.com/condos-for-sale/the-lakes/).

#### Why buyers choose The Lakes

- **Water everywhere you look.** Lakes, streams and koi ponds run through the grounds, and many units look out on them.
- **Walk to errands and schools.** Piazza Carmel is about 5 minutes on foot, and the elementary and middle schools are within half a mile.
- **No Mello-Roos.** Older construction means no special tax on top of the property tax — a real monthly saving next to newer communities.

*HOA*

### The Lakes HOA: Fee & Amenities

One monthly fee covers the grounds, the water features and the amenities.

$560–$599/month

**HOA fee** 2025 sales listed $560–$565; every 2026 listing shows $599, so expect about $599 now. Confirm the current fee for a specific unit.

#### Amenities included

- Five lakes & koi ponds
- Pool & spa
- Tennis & pickleball courts
- Walking paths & dog area
- BBQ area & community room
- Covered carport & storage

**Also covered:** landscaping, exterior building maintenance and common-area upkeep. Units have in-unit laundry, and there is EV charging and guest parking.

#### How The Lakes's HOA Compares

- **The Lakes:** $560–$599/mo
- **Martinique:** $428–$500/mo
- **Arborlake:** $450–$460/mo
- **Camino Villas:** $375–$450/mo
- **Carmel Pointe:** $340–$433/mo
- **Del Mar Villas:** $330–$370/mo

The Lakes' HOA is on the high side for nearby condos, but there's no Mello-Roos, which narrows the gap with newer communities. Ranges are from 2025–2026 MLS listings.

*Find Your Fit*

### Is The Lakes the Right Community for You?

Who it suits best, and the honest tradeoffs to weigh before you buy.

#### A great fit for

- **First-Time Buyers** — One of the lowest price points in 92130, with no Mello-Roos and top-rated schools within walking distance.
- **Downsizers** — Single-level living, HOA-managed grounds, and dinner at Piazza Carmel or One Paseo without driving.
- **Investors** — Steady rental demand from the SR-56 and Sorrento Valley job centers, and no Mello-Roos in the numbers.

#### Tradeoffs to weigh

- **Carport parking, no garages** — Each unit has a reserved covered carport space with storage, but there are no garages.
- **Higher HOA than nearby condos** — About $599/mo in 2026, more than Arborlake or Carmel Pointe. Ask what reserves and recent projects look like.
- **1980s buildings** — Built in 1984–1985; interiors range from original to fully updated, so compare finishes carefully.
- **Few 3-bedrooms** — Almost every sale is a 1- or 2-bedroom; for more space, look at Chateau Village or The Groves next door.

*Good to Know*

### The Lakes Condo FAQs

#### What is the price range for The Lakes condos?

Recent sales at The Lakes ranged from about $630,000 to $935,000. By size: 1-bedrooms $630K–$670K (median $655K; 4 sales in the last 12 months) and 2-bedrooms $808K–$935K (median $850K; the last 3 sales, since Nov 2024). Condition, floor level and location in the community explain most of the gap. Ask for a current comparison before you make an offer.

#### What are the HOA fees at The Lakes?

MLS listings show $560–$599 per month: 2025 sales listed $560–$565, and every 2026 listing shows $599. The fee covers the pool, spa, tennis and pickleball courts, the lakes and koi ponds, landscaping, exterior maintenance and the community room. Confirm the current fee for a specific unit.

#### Does The Lakes have Mello-Roos?

No. None of the recent MLS listings at The Lakes show a Mello-Roos assessment, and the property tax rate is about 1.07% of assessed value.

#### How big are the units at The Lakes?

From about 791 sq ft (1-bedroom) to 1,269 sq ft (2-bedroom). Most 1-bedrooms are 790–950 sq ft and most 2-bedrooms are 1,100–1,270 sq ft.

#### What is parking like at The Lakes?

Each unit has a reserved covered carport space with extra storage, plus guest parking and EV charging stations. There are no garages.

#### How quickly do The Lakes condos sell?

About 8 homes a year have sold here over the last 5 years. The median time on market was about 12 days, so well-priced units go quickly.

#### How does The Lakes compare to other Carmel Valley condo communities?

The Lakes and neighboring Arborlake are the two Carmel Valley condo communities built around water. The Lakes is a few years older, sells at similar prices, has a higher HOA ($560–$599 vs. $450–$460) and carport parking. Carmel Pointe is newer with garage parking and a lower HOA.

### Life at Del Mar Villas

Del Mar Villas was built in 1990 as an apartment community and became condominiums in 2004. That history explains two things buyers notice right away: grounds with more than 30 years of mature trees and lawn, and an amenity list larger than most Carmel Valley condo complexes at this price. Every home is a single-level flat with its own patio or balcony.

#### Why buyers choose Del Mar Villas

- **Walk to school.** Carmel Del Mar Elementary and Carmel Valley Middle School are each about 0.3 miles away, and Torrey Pines High is about a mile.
- **Walk to everything else.** The recreation center and library, Piazza Carmel, One Paseo and Del Mar Highlands Town Center are all within a 12-minute walk.
- **Low monthly dues.** Dues of about $330–$370 a month are among the lowest of any Carmel Valley condo community, and they cover water and trash.

[Get my Del Mar Villas home value](https://www.carmelvalleycondos.com/home-value/#valuation-form) [Call Sez · (858) 436-6585](tel:+18584366585)

*Find Your Fit*

### Is Del Mar Villas the Right Community for You?

Who it suits best, and the honest tradeoffs to weigh before you buy.

#### A great fit for

- **Families** — Two schools about a third of a mile away, at a price well below Carmel Valley single-family homes.
- **First-Time Buyers** — 1-bedrooms have sold for under $600K, with low monthly dues and big-community amenities.
- **Investors** — Steady rental demand from school-zone families and the SR-56 job corridor, and dues that cover water and trash.

#### Tradeoffs to weigh

- **Smaller homes** — Plans run 638–950 sq ft, and there are no 3-bedrooms. For more room, look at nearby townhomes such as Elysian.
- **Covered parking, no garages** — Homes come with covered parking and storage, not private garages.
- **Interiors vary a lot** — Built in 1990 and converted in 2004, so some homes are fully redone and others are close to original. The price gap can reach $100K.
- **Mello-Roos** — A small special tax, about $366–$452 a year, on top of the property tax.

*Good to Know*

### Del Mar Villas Carmel Valley FAQs

#### How much do Del Mar Villas Carmel Valley homes sell for?

Recent sales at Del Mar Villas ranged from about $593,000 to $700,000. By size: 1-bedrooms $593K–$599K (median $599K; 3 sales in the last 24 months) and 2-bedrooms $664K–$700K (median $684K; 4 sales in the last 24 months). Condition, floor level and location in the community explain most of the gap. Ask for a current comparison before you make an offer.

#### What are the monthly dues at Del Mar Villas?

MLS listings show $330–$370 a month: 2025 sales listed $330–$365, and the 2026 listings show $370. The dues cover water, trash, landscaping, exterior and roof maintenance, and the pool, spa, sauna, fitness center, courts and clubhouse. Confirm the current amount for a specific home.

#### Does Del Mar Villas have Mello-Roos?

Yes, a small one: about $366–$452 a year, or roughly $30–$38 a month. Few listings report it, so check the tax bill for the specific home. The base property tax rate is about 1.07% of the purchase price.

#### Are Del Mar Villas homes condos or townhomes?

They're condominiums, not townhomes. Every home is a single-level flat on one floor, either a ground-floor or an upper-floor unit, with a private patio or balcony.

#### How big are the homes at Del Mar Villas?

There are three floor plans: a 638 sq ft 1-bedroom, 1-bath, and two 2-bedroom, 2-bath plans of about 864 and 950 sq ft.

#### What is parking like at Del Mar Villas?

Homes come with covered parking and a storage space. There are no private garages.

#### How quickly do Del Mar Villas condos sell?

The median time on market over the last 5 years was about 20 days, so well-priced homes usually go under contract within three weeks.

#### I own at Del Mar Villas. What affects my sale price most?

Condition. Because the buildings date from 1990, buyers compare finishes closely, and a fully updated home can sell for $100K or more above one in original condition. Floor plan and location within the grounds matter next. I can show you which recent sales are true comparisons for your home.

### Condo & Townhome Prices by Year

Closed condo and townhome sales in Carmel Valley San Diego 92130, by calendar year.

| Year | Homes Sold | Median Sale Price | Avg. Price / Sq Ft | Avg. Days on Market | Sale vs. Original List |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026 (Jan 1 – Oct 22) | 98 | $995,000 | $815 | 32 | 97.9% |
| 2025 | 151 | $970,000 | $815 | 30 | 98.4% |
| 2024 | 143 | $970,000 | $838 | 19 | 100.0% |
| 2023 | 139 | $969,000 | $790 | 28 | 100.0% |
| 2022 | 180 | $942,500 | $799 | 16 | 102.2% |

Condos and townhomes are reported together as attached homes, since listing agents frequently enter a townhome as a condo — or the reverse — in the MLS. Source: closed sales reported in the MLS for zip code 92130, January 3, 2022 – October 22, 2026, compiled by Sez Sezer, Keller Williams Realty. 2026 is year to date.

*What It Means*

### Reading the Carmel Valley Condo Market

#### For Buyers

The median condo and townhome price has climbed from $942,500 in 2022 to $995,000 year to date in 2026 — a gain of roughly 5.6% over five years, far steadier than the swings seen in detached single-family homes over the same stretch. Days on market in 2026 sit at 32, up from the 16-19 day pace of 2022-2024, giving buyers a bit more room to evaluate HOA financials and unit condition before competing.

#### For Sellers

Price per square foot has held in the high-$700s to low-$800s range every year since 2022, with 2026 pricing right in line with 2025. Units are still selling close to original list price — 97.9% to 100% most years — which means overpricing, not a soft market, is the main thing costing sellers time on market. A well-priced, well-presented condo in an established Carmel Valley community is still moving in roughly a month or less.

*Good to Know*

### Market Report FAQ

#### What is the median price for a condo or townhome in Carmel Valley?

The median sale price for Carmel Valley condos and townhomes in 92130 is $995,000 year to date in 2026, based on 98 closed sales, up from a median of $970,000 in 2025.

#### Why are condos and townhomes reported together?

Listing agents frequently enter a townhome as a condo in the MLS, or the reverse, so the two property types are reported together as "attached homes" to keep the year-over-year data consistent and accurate.

#### How fast are Carmel Valley condos selling right now?

Condos and townhomes averaged 32 days on market in 2026 year to date, up slightly from 2024's 19-day average, but still selling at 97.9% of original list price — a sign that well-priced units continue to move efficiently.

#### Is now a good time to buy or sell a Carmel Valley condo?

Prices have risen steadily and days on market remain reasonable by historical standards, which tends to favor sellers who price accurately and buyers who are prepared to move quickly on well-presented units. The right strategy depends on your specific community and timeline — reach out for a tailored read on your situation.
